## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * Optimized Docker builds with multi-stage approach for smaller, more efficient images
  * Added automatic version stamping via commit SHA for build traceability
  * Enhanced Docker image security by running as non-root user
  * Updated CI/CD workflows to support version tracking

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Walkthrough

This PR refactors Docker image building and package versioning from a single-stage model with `IS_RELEASE` flags to a multi-stage architecture using git commit SHA (`VERSION_SHA`). GitHub Actions workflows now capture the short commit SHA and pass it as a build argument through Docker to `bin/jam/build-for-npm.sh`. The Dockerfile converts to a builder stage (full dependencies, compile, production-only install) and runtime stage (non-root user, compiled bundle only, direct `index.js` entrypoint). Build scripts across convert, jam, and lib layers update to stamp package versions from `VERSION_SHA` instead of conditional git hashing. The jam build worker flattening logic is refactored into a reusable function. The old `start.sh` entrypoint is removed, and documentation is updated.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~25 minutes

## Possibly related PRs

- [FluffyLabs/typeberry#619](https://github.com/FluffyLabs/typeberry/pull/619): Both PRs modify the `Dockerfile` to run the app under a non-root user.
- [FluffyLabs/typeberry#666](https://github.com/FluffyLabs/typeberry/pull/666): Both PRs modify npm packaging/version-stamping scripts to change how build version is computed, replacing git-based or flag-based logic with environment variable versioning.
